transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start time: 15:30 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Rocio Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Ethan Ross, Priya Kapoor, Derek Wu, Samira Ali (StratusWorks)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot economics: tokens/sec per dollar, caching wins observed in week 2, and batching tradeoffs for latency sensitive flows. Agreed action items for benchmark runs and security docs.

Topics covered:
- Week 2 pilot results snapshot (tokens/sec/$, observed latency distributions)
- Prefix/KV cache savings and warm vs cold hit rates
- Batching: dynamic batching thresholds and tail latency concerns
- Quantization and model variants to reduce unit cost
- Security/ops: VPC, KMS, audit logs, retention

Transcript:
[00:00] Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thank you for joining. Quick roll call — we have Ethan, Priya, Derek and Samira from Stratus, and Liam and Rocio from our side. Cool. We're about 40 minutes. We'll go over the week two econ numbers and then plan the benchmark work.

[00:22] Speaker 2 (Ethan): Thanks Maya. Quick note, we're joining from SF and have to jump at 16:10 so if we can capture next steps that'd be great.

[00:32] Liam (SE): Alright so I shared the dashboard earlier, the headline — tokens per dollar improved about 18% week-over-week after enabling prefix cache for the FAQ flow. That was mostly from a 65% cache-hit for the 1.2k prompt prefix.

[00:50] Priya: Sorry, can you say "prefix cache" again? we call it, like, preface cash at times in the team, so want to make sure it's the same?

[00:58] Liam: Yeah, prefix cache, K-V cache — the thing that stores key/value attention states so we don't re-compute for repeated starting text. Sometimes the transcript says K-V cash, haha.

[01:10] Derek: Right. We saw a drop in token spend on our side too, approx 16% on the webchat flow. But curious — what's the story for higher-latency, search-style queries where caching won't help?

[01:28] Liam: Good question. For non-repeated queries caching is minimal, so we rely on batching and smaller model variants. On our metrics, batching helps tokens/sec but increases p95 by about 40-60ms depending on batch window. There is a cost/latency sweet spot.

[01:48] Rocio (CSM): I'll flag that the customer-facing dashboard now shows tokens/sec per dollar and p50/p95 latency columns. That helped surface the tradeoffs for Priya's team.

[02:02] Ethan: Can you walk the team through the exact tokens/sec per dollar calc? We want to map to our CFO's unit-econ model.

[02:12] Liam: Sure — high level: we take total tokens served over the measurement window, divide by total infra cost (gpu runtime + host fees + egress) for that window. We report tokens per USD. We also calculate tokens per second per USD for throughput-oriented flows. Example: with cache on, FAQ flow was at ~120k tokens / $ for the week; without cache it was ~100k. Throughput in tokens/sec rose from 450 -> 540 when we allowed a 50ms batch window.

[02:44] Samira: Where does quantization fit into that? We've been nervous about quality drop for int8 on longer contexts.

[02:52] Liam: Right now our q8 profile shows 12-20% cost saving versus bf16 for generation-heavy traces. Latency improves slightly as compute per token drops. But for some of your longer-doc summarization prompts we saw small regressions in factuality in the eval set — not catastrophic but noticeable. We recommend running a short quality check on your 3 worst-case prompts if you want to try int8.

[03:18] Priya: We'll do that. We'll identify one canonical prompt per flow.

[03:24] Maya: On routing — we proposed a fallback policy: route to dedicated model variant under high load and to hosted smaller variant for non-sensitive workloads. Ethan, is your regulatory constraint? I remember you said some PII workflows need VPC/on-prem later in the roadmap.

[03:38] Ethan: Correct. PII flows must stay in VPC and we need KMS integration for customer-managed keys. For the pilot, the majority is non-PII but we want us to validate the VPC path.

[03:48] Derek: On that note, network egress — if we pin to region X, we still have a 3% additional egress cost. We'll need to bake that into the tokens per dollar model.

[03:58] Liam: Good catch. Our cost calc we sent earlier had a line item for egress but we can break it out by region in the updated sheet.

[04:10] Speaker 3 (Priya): Also curious about batching policy complexity — if we batch aggressively, onboarding frontend engineers say it increases tail latency on interactive flows and hurts user experience. How do we mitigate?

[04:22] Liam: Two mitigations — dynamic batching (shorter windows for interactive routes), and client-side speculative responses (token streaming earlier) so the UI feels snappier. Also we can pin low-latency flows to smaller batch sizes or to dedicated capacity.

[04:40] Ethan: Do you have a recommended threshold for batch window? Our current target for product is p95 < 350ms for chat.

[04:48] Liam: Empirically we've found 10-30ms windows give a good tokens/sec improvement without moving p95 beyond 350ms on medium-size models. For stricter SLOs you'd go towards 5ms windows or dedicated instances. We can show the sensitivity curve in the next report.

[05:05] Priya: That sounds sensible. Can you also show me the pre-warm strategy? We have upticks during morning hours and cold starts are painful.

[05:14] Liam: We recommend a light keep-alive traffic pattern and aggressive KV warming for the top 1k prefixes. That recovered warm hit rates from 40% to 63% in our run. Warm hit rate is the big lever for token savings.

[05:32] Samira: On SSO and audit logs — our security team will need to see RBAC, SAML config, and audit log retention. How quickly can we get those docs?

[05:40] Maya: We'll send SOC2 summary, SAML SSO guide, and KMS integration notes by Friday. Rocio will attach the audit log schema and retention options.

[05:52] Rocio: Adding that. Also we'll include sample logs to show token-level tracing and per-route cost attribution.

[06:04] Ethan: Great. Back to numbers — Liam, you said 18% improvement with prefix caching. Do you have absolute cost per 1M tokens?

[06:12] Liam: Yes. On the model variant we used: bf16 baseline was ~$0.95 per 1M tokens rendered, with cache on effective cost for that flow dropped to ~$0.78 per 1M. Int8 runs were down to ~$0.64 but again quality caveats. Those numbers include infra amortization for the test window.

[06:32] Priya: CFO will want worst-case and best-case for scaling to 10 million daily tokens. Could you run projections in the sheet?

[06:40] Maya: We'll add scale scenarios: base, cached-heavy, and worst-case no-cache.

[06:46] Derek: One operational issue — our platform team wants to ensure graceful degradation when a region loses capacity. Does Redwood support automatic fallback to smaller model variants in another region?

[06:56] Liam: Yes, we support policy-based routing with automatic fallback to compatible variants. You can define latency or cost thresholds. There is a small additional cross-region egress cost but in our tests failover time is ~6-12s depending on KV warm state.

[07:12] Ethan: 6-12s failover — okay. That might be acceptable if we have a buffering strategy.

[07:18] Priya: Let's talk about the benchmark plan — what's the minimum set we should run this week to validate tokens/sec/$ claims?

[07:26] Liam: Minimum: 1) baseline bf16 run with no cache, 2) prefix cache enabled run, 3) int8 quant run, 4) batching window sensitivity runs (5ms, 20ms, 50ms). Each should run for at least 30 minutes to get stable tail metrics. We'll use your sampled prompts for better fidelity.

[07:48] Maya: We'll also do a short 1-hour end-to-end pass that simulates morning ramp. That should uncover warm/cold dynamics.

[07:58] Samira: For the test VPC, what's required from us? Derek or Priya, do we have network contacts?

[08:06] Derek: I'll open the ticket and share the peering details by Friday.

[08:12] Maya: Perfect. Next — pricing cadence. We're proposing a blended model for pilot: per-token with a small reserved capacity discount if you hit the commit threshold. I'll send the exact numbers.

[08:24] Ethan: Do you have any examples of customers who hit commit thresholds and the realized unit cost? Not the name but ranges?

[08:30] Maya: We can provide anonymized ranges — typically another 10-18% reduction after a 3-month committed capacity contract.

[08:38] Priya: One more question on observability: can you break cost by route and by model variant? We want to see per-feature unit economics.

[08:48] Rocio: Yes, route-level dashboards are available. We'll share a sample export that maps tokens, token-cost, and latency per route.

[08:56] Ethan: OK good. We're mostly concerned about the conversational chat route and the nightly summarization job which is long context. Both behave differently.

[09:06] Liam: For the nightly summarization, caching won't help much but quantization plus batching works well there because latency SLOs are relaxed. So it's a prime candidate for int8.

[09:18] Priya: Sounds like a plan. Can we also look at a hybrid: chat uses cache + small batch + bf16; summarization uses int8 + large batch.

[09:28] Liam: Exactly, that's the routing policy we typically recommend.

[09:34] Ethan: Anything else on data residency? We noted you have private deployment options but what's the ETA for an on-prem package if we need it?

[09:42] Maya: Our Private offering is available for enterprise customers, typical onboarding is 6-10 weeks including KMS/HSM integrations and network setup. For pilots we recommend VPC mode which can be faster.

[09:56] Derek: For the pilot's acceptance criteria: 1) tokens/sec/$ within 15% of projections after tuning, 2) p95 under 350ms for chat, 3) successful VPC peering test. We need those in writing.

[10:12] Maya: We'll write up the acceptance criteria and attach to the pilot plan doc.

[10:20] Rocio: I'll add those as acceptance checklist items and share with everyone.

[10:28] Ethan: OK we are at 16:08, I need to jump. Thanks all.

[10:34] Maya: Quick recap — action items: Liam runs the benchmark matrix, Priya provides prompts, Derek opens network ticket, Maya sends pricing and security docs, Rocio shares dashboard export. We'll target the due dates in the notes.

[10:48] Priya: Thanks, appreciate it.

[10:52] Liam: One last note — we'll also include a small spreadsheet that shows tokens/sec/$ sensitivity to batch size and cache-hit rate so CFO can see upside/downside.

[11:05] Maya: Great. Ending and we'll follow up in email with calendar invites for the benchmark slot.

Action items (as discussed):
- Liam to run the benchmark matrix (bf16, q8, int8, batch windows) — due 2026-04-09
- Priya to provide canonical prompts and one long-context exemplar — due 2026-04-08
- Derek to open ticket for VPC peering and share egress constraints — due 2026-04-10
- Maya to send pricing and SOC2/KMS security docs — due 2026-04-08
- Rocio to export per-route cost/latency dashboard and share sample logs — due 2026-04-09

Recording notes / transcription quirks: occasional mis-hearings of acronyms (K-V cache seen as K-V cash), filler words and slight speaker attribution errors in first 30s.
